title: SUM: total a column
prompt: In B5, total Q1 revenue for all three regions with one function.

hints.syntax: Start with = and close every bracket: =SUM(B2:B4).
hints.func-sum: Add the three cells with SUM instead of typing 1200+1450+930.
hints.require-ref: Your answer has to point at the Q1 cells, not repeat a total you worked out yourself.
hints.value: Close, but that is not the Q1 total. Check that the range covers all three regions and none of the Q2 column.
hints.error: SUM only fails on what you feed it: #VALUE! means a cell in the range holds text instead of a number, #REF! means the range was pointed at something deleted. Re-select B2:B4 and let Excel write the range for you.

docs.explain: SUM adds up every number you point it at. Here the Q1 column holds 1200, 1450 and 930, and SUM(B2:B4) returns 3580 because 1200 + 1450 + 930 = 3580. Nothing has to be typed twice: change the South figure to 1500 and the total follows, which is the entire reason a spreadsheet exists. SUM ignores text and empty cells inside a range, so a stray label in the middle of a column will not break the answer — the trap is the other way around, a number stored as text, which SUM silently skips. If a region is missing from the total, look for a left-aligned number in the column.

errors.text: You passed a cell that holds text where SUM expected a number, usually by summing the Region column instead of the Q1 column.
The function name is misspelled, for example SUMM or SU. Excel does not guess.
SUM(B2:B5) would add the label cell B5 as well, which is how a total quietly doubles itself in real files.

docs.atWork: Every monthly close starts like this: one row per branch, one column per period, and a total at the bottom. The people who get promoted are the ones whose totals update themselves.
docs.outcome: Total a column with one function instead of typing every cell.
